title: [CI] Move MSVC C++ code analysis into a parallel CI job

proposed_comments.title: Keep analysis enabled when no parallel replacement runs
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep analysis enabled when no parallel replacement runs

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `.pipelines/v2/templates/pipeline-ci-build.yml` (the build-job variables and `CppCodeAnalysis` stage), `.pipelines/v2/ci-nightly.yml`, and the WebView2/Windows App SDK variant callers.

**Problem:** The build jobs now set `SkipCppCodeAnalysis: 1` unconditionally, but the replacement stage runs only when `runCppCodeAnalysis` is true, which defaults to false. `ci.yml` opts in; `ci-test-with-canary-webview2.yml` and `ci-using-the-latest-winappsdk.yml` do not. Those variant pipelines therefore lose their inline C++ analysis without receiving the parallel replacement.

**Why it matters:** If left unfixed, variant builds can pass without running the analysis that previously checked them, allowing variant-specific diagnostics to go undetected. This is a coverage gap, not evidence that a particular diagnostic currently fails.

**Suggested change:**
1. Make the ordinary-build skip conditional on the parallel analysis stage being enabled.
2. Preserve the nightly prewarm's deliberate build/cache-input parity with an explicit false-by-default override, such as `skipCppCodeAnalysisInBuild`. Set it only in `ci-nightly.yml`, and skip inline analysis when either that override or `runCppCodeAnalysis` is true.
3. Keep the main PR pipeline's parallel analysis blocking, while leaving inline analysis enabled for the WebView2/Windows App SDK variants unless they explicitly gain a replacement stage. Do not remove the callee's existing `variables` template parameter or its job-variable insertion.

**Verification:** Check the four callers separately: main skips inline analysis and runs the parallel stage; nightly retains its explicit cache-prewarm skip; both variants retain inline analysis. Check all four boolean combinations, validate the expanded Azure pipeline templates, and run `.pipelines/tests/mwbUiTestSelection.Tests.ps1` to preserve the adjacent selector behavior.

**Current-revision reassessment:** The SDK setup simplification and ARM64 HID gating changes do not change this relationship: both variants still inherit the false analysis-stage default while the build skip remains unconditional. Earlier executable checks retain their original revision identities; this refresh rechecked the exact template and all four callers, not a new Azure run.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: Coordinated template and nightly-caller changes must preserve cache-prewarm parity; presented as one implementation-ready general PR comment instead of separate code suggestions.

confidence.rationale: Current-head template and caller source still shows the unconditional skip, false default and gated replacement. Earlier corrected-structure and 28 selector checks remain bound to their actual original inputs; live Azure expansion and execution on this rebased head were not performed.
